evidence: Frozen startLoading invokes handler.start under stateLock. Its unknown-scope path calls URLProtocolClient.didFail under the lock too.
respond marks finished and calls client didReceive/didLoad/didFinish under NSRecursiveLock. stop callback itself is already outside the lock.

NSRecursiveLock permits same-thread recursion only. If an external callback waits for another thread to call stopLoading, that thread waits for the held mutex. Existing direct same-thread tests do not exercise this liveness boundary.
Setting finished before notifications prevents stopLoading from changing cancellation state during a response sequence.
source_liveness_risk.certainty: External-callback-under-lock is established by source and admits a deterministic cross-thread regression. Actual CFNetwork deadlock as cause of every native timeout is unproved without that regression or thread traces.
action: Add bounded deterministic regressions where start handler and client receive callback request stopLoading on another thread and await its return. Old helper should fail without an indefinite hang.
Move external handler/client calls outside the mutex, including unknown-scope failure. Preserve responding/stopped/finished state and cancellation checks between client notifications.
Keep retired scopes fail-closed, original timing bounds and overfulfill detection. Production transport consent logic need not change to repair this helper boundary.
